name: Kim Clijsters
milestone_by_age_26: Won her first WTA singles title at the Luxembourg Open in September 1999 at age 16, also reaching the Wimbledon fourth round and earning WTA Newcomer of the Year the same year.
early_history_summary: Clijsters began playing tennis at age five after her father built a clay court at their home. By nine she was training fifteen hours per week under coach Benny Vanhoudt, and at thirteen she joined the Flemish Tennis Association program in Antwerp under Carl Maes. She turned professional in 1997 at age fourteen and rose from a ranking of 409 to 47 within two years.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Lei Clijsters, a professional soccer player who won the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup in 1988 and earned 40 caps for Belgium, and Els Vandecaetsbeek, a Belgian national gymnastics champion. Her father built a clay tennis court at their home when she was five.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were accomplished professional athletes: father a top-flight Belgian footballer, mother a national gymnastics champion. This provided genetic athletic endowment, sports culture immersion, and the resources to build a home tennis court.

Her father built a clay court at home when she was five, and by nine she was training fifteen hours weekly under a dedicated coach. She joined the Flemish Tennis Association's elite program at thirteen and turned professional at fourteen, winning her first WTA title at sixteen. The combination of athletic heritage, early facilities, and intensive coaching created a clear pathway to early success.

name: Avi Loeb

He pursued graduate research in plasma physics at the Soreq Nuclear Research Center, earning his PhD at 24 — the first PhD in the Talpiot program — while leading a weapons research project that received international SDI funding.

name: Arturo Pomar

World Champion Alexander Alekhine took personal interest in Pomar, giving him special lessons, and at thirteen Pomar drew against Alekhine in a tournament game that lasted over seventy moves. He won his first Spanish Championship at fourteen in 1946.
family_context_summary: Born in Palma de Mallorca, Spain. Learned chess by watching his father play his grandfather at home. Family faced economic hardship in post-civil war Spain; Pomar helped support his family by playing simultaneous exhibitions.

evidence_summary: Pomar learned chess at five by watching his father and grandfather play at home in Palma de Mallorca. name: Sergei Polunin
milestone_by_age_26: Became the Royal Ballet's youngest ever male principal dancer in June 2010 at age 20, after winning the Prix de Lausanne in 2006 at 17 and being named Young British Dancer of the Year in 2007.
early_history_summary: Polunin started gymnastics at age four in Kherson, Ukraine, then switched to ballet at eight. He attended the Kyiv State Choreographic College, with his mother moving to Kyiv with him while his father worked in Portugal to fund the training. At thirteen he joined the Royal Ballet School in London, sponsored by the Rudolf Nureyev Foundation, and rapidly ascended to first soloist by 2009 and principal by 2010.
family_context_summary: Born in Kherson, Ukraine to a poor family. His mother Galina moved with him to Kyiv for ballet training, while his father Vladimir worked as a builder in Portugal and his grandmother went to Greece to financially support the family. Parents divorced when Polunin was fifteen due to the strain of separation.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family ballet background. Mother recognized his talent and saw ballet as an escape from poverty, making extraordinary sacrifices including family separation across Europe to fund training.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, family sacrifice, Royal Ballet School, Nureyev Foundation scholarship, Prix de Lausanne, prodigy
evidence_summary: Polunin grew up in desperate poverty in Kherson, Ukraine, where his family scattered across Europe — father to Portugal, grandmother to Greece — to fund his ballet training. His mother moved with him to Kyiv, living in one room for four years. At thirteen, he earned a Rudolf Nureyev Foundation-sponsored place at the Royal Ballet School in London. His combination of natural physical talent and the elite Royal Ballet pipeline propelled him to become the youngest ever male principal at twenty. The extreme family sacrifice and pressure eventually contributed to his parents' divorce and his own turbulent relationship with ballet.
